properties.chose:
VALIDATE ARGUMENTS AGAINST THE PUBLISHED SCHEMA BEFORE DESERIALIZING. Wrong type, missing and unknown fields then all refuse naming the tool and the full field path, nested ones included. Widen the refusal gate to cover the whole class, not instances.

The false "the schema publishes no description" hint is fixed in the same change: it reads only top-level properties, and 22 of 35 required nested fields are described.

Rejected: matching more serde phrasings. That extends the hand-kept list that missed this class.

Anthony, 2026-10-02: "I accept all your recommendations."
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02, idea 15 ("Refusal shape: the refusal_speaks gate should cover bare deserialize errors"). Triaged 2026-10-02 by triage agent C.

THE QUESTION: on 0.77.0, an argument of the wrong JSON type is refused on every tool with serde's bare "failed to deserialize parameters: invalid type: …". It names neither the tool nor the field (fact:root-cause-a-wrong-type-argument-is-refused-in-the-bare-serde-string-because-the-interception-matches-two-phrasings-2026-10-02). Since 2026-09-11 the call_tool interception rewrites only "missing field" and "unknown field", and refusal_speaks.py probes only those two. How far should the fix reach?

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) MATCH MORE PHRASINGS: add "invalid type", "invalid value" and "invalid length" arms to the interception, prefixing the tool's name. Cheap. It still cannot name the FIELD, because serde_json's type error carries no path, and it is the instance pattern that left this class open after 2026-09-11.
(b) DESERIALISE WITH A PATH: run each tool's parameters through path tracking (for example serde_path_to_error) at the router, so the refusal reads "`external_dependency`: `components` must be a list of strings; got the string "core"". It covers the class at one point, but it means owning the step rmcp's Parameters extractor does today.
(c) CHECK AGAINST THE PUBLISHED SCHEMA FIRST: validate the arguments against the tool's own input schema before deserialising, and refuse with the JSON pointer, the expected type and the schema's description of the field. One source of truth with what find_tools and describe would serve. It costs a schema validator in the hot path.
(d) WIDEN THE GATE whatever the fix: for every served tool, refusal_speaks.py sends one wrong-typed value per typed parameter, generated from the schema, and requires the tool's name and the field's name in the refusal. The usage ledger gains the invalid_argument class owed since fact:the-first-real-usage-report-classed-four-of-five-refusals-as-other.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept:
- An MCP client already knows which tool it called, so the tool name matters most to the --call door, a batch, and a log reader. But the field name matters everywhere.
- (b) and (c) add work to every call for an error a schema-reading client should never make.
- The door could name the tool on its exit-2 path for free (it already does on exit 1), which answers part of the report with no server change.
properties.name: ACCEPTED 2026-10-02 — every argument refusal names the tool and the field path: arguments are checked against the published schema before deserializing
properties.rationale: Recorded open because (a) is the cheap repeat of an instance fix, and (b)/(c) are the class fix with a real cost and a dependency on how far reflow2 wants to own rmcp's argument step. The 2026-09-11 lesson, that a wire-level gate is what keeps a refusal honest, argues for (d) whichever fix is taken.
